    level="1"
    right="Feat 16"
    pfs=""
>
[Vigorous Victor](/Feats.aspx?ID=8161) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star](/Sources.aspx?ID=283) pg. 79

**Archetype** [Heroic Scion](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=339)

**Prerequisites**
[Heroic Scion Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8151)

</column>

---

Long years of success have not only shown you where your limits lie, they’ve expanded them. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to saving throws against effects that would cause you to become [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68), [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71), [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=73), [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91), or [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92). Whenever you attempt such a save, you can spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3323) do so at mythic proficiency. The bonus increases to +3 at 18th level.

[Viking Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2094) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 198

**Archetype** [Viking](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=81)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3)

</column>

---

Vikings spend long periods of time at sea, only to leap from their boats at a moment's notice, charge through the surf, and take their enemies by storm. You're trained in [Sailing Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8). When moving through water using your land Speed, you ignore difficult terrain resulting from shallow water, such as in bogs or on beaches. In addition, if you roll a success for your [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check to [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=39), you get a critical success instead.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the viking archetype.

<title level="2">Viking Dedication leads to...</title>
[Hurling Charge](/Feats.aspx?ID=2095), [Second Shield](/Feats.aspx?ID=2098), [Viking Vindicator](/Feats.aspx?ID=3619), [Viking Weapon Familiarity](/Feats.aspx?ID=2096)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Viking Vindicator](/Feats.aspx?ID=3619) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Knights of Lastwall](/Sources.aspx?ID=123) pg. 81

**Archetype** [Viking](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=81)

**Prerequisites**
[Viking Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2094)

**Access**
Knights of Lastwall have access to this feat.

</column>

---

You are one of the raiders eagerly planning to launch an assault by sea on the Whispering Tyrant's Isle of Terror. You gain the [Sudden Charge](/Feats.aspx?ID=134) fighter feat, though it's a viking feat for you instead. As normal when gaining an additional feat from an archetype feat, gaining Sudden Charge doesn't count toward fulfilling the special requirement for Viking Dedication. If you already had Sudden Charge, you can retrain it as part of gaining this feat. When you use Sudden Charge to Strike a target in shallow water, the target is [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) against your Strike, as you use the water kicked up by your passage to camouflage your angle of attack. If you have [Viking Weapon Familiarity](/Feats.aspx?ID=2096) or [Viking Weapon Specialist](/Feats.aspx?ID=2097), add the [bastard sword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=15) and [rapier](/Weapons.aspx?ID=36) to the list of weapons in those feats.

From childhood, you have been exposed to traditional viking combat techniques, and you soon learned to handle axe, sword, and shield in battle. Now, you can raid proudly alongside your fellows. You gain the [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=5212) reaction. Additionally, you have familiarity with the [battle axe](/Weapons.aspx?ID=371), [hatchet](/Weapons.aspx?ID=382), [longsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=386), [shield boss](/Weapons.aspx?ID=396), [shield spikes](/Weapons.aspx?ID=397), and [shortsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=398)—for the purposes of proficiency, you treat any of these weapons as simple weapons. 

At 5th level, whenever you get a critical hit with one of these weapons, you get its [critical specialization effect](/WeaponGroups.aspx).

Your church ensures that you are cared for. You can use [Religion](/Rules.aspx?ID=2976) to [Coerce](/Actions.aspx?ID=2394), [Gather Information](/Actions.aspx?ID=2391), [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=2392), or make a [Request](/Actions.aspx?ID=2393) as long as you are in a town or city with a church dedicated to your deity. If the target of the check is also a worshipper of your deity or is your hunted prey, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to the check.

<title level="2">Vindicator Dedication leads to...</title>
[Call The Hunt](/Feats.aspx?ID=7260), [Interrogate](/Feats.aspx?ID=7257), [Silence the Profane (Vindicator)](/Feats.aspx?ID=7258), [Vindicator's Judgement](/Feats.aspx?ID=7259)

You attempt a saving throw against a spell

Those who seek to do you personal harm with magic must suffer the same misfortune. Before you attempt your saving throw, spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3323). You make this saving throw at mythic proficiency. On any result but a critical failure, the spell’s caster takes 10d6 mental damage (basic Will save against your class DC or spell DC using mythic proficiency, whichever is higher). At 18th level, the mental damage increases to 11d6, and at 20th level, the mental damage increases to 12d6.

    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Virtuosic Dancer](/Feats.aspx?ID=7639) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Curtain Call</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #204: Stage Fright](/Sources.aspx?ID=245) pg. 82

**Archetype** [Acrobat](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=236) (Level 12)

**Prerequisites**
[Acrobat Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6240)

</column>

---

You're so fond of using your Acrobatic feats on the stage that you've begun adding your own flair to these dances on the big stage. When you Perform, if you do a performance that is either related to dance, acting or opera, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to the roll. If you're legendary in [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34), this increases to a +2 circumstance bonus. You gain the Dancing Dodge reaction. 

**Dancing Dodge** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([move](/Traits.aspx?ID=658)) **Trigger** You're hit by a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) during the first round of combat; **Effect** You take advantage of the fact that your foe isn't ready to anticipate your dance-like moves in combat. Add a +3 circumstance bonus to your Armor Class against the triggering Strike to determine the Strike's actual result.

---

You've found a way to use a hodgepodge combination of devices to enhance your visual abilities in every situation. You gain [darkvision](/Rules.aspx?ID=415) and [low-light vision](/Rules.aspx?ID=416), and you can see [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=26) creatures and objects as translucent shapes, though these shapes are indistinct enough to be [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) to you.

 If an effect would give you the [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=1) condition, the effect must attempt a [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) check against your class DC, with your counteract level equaling half your level, rounded up. On a failed counteract check, you aren't blinded—your various devices are able to compensate.

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #168: King of the Mountain](/Sources.aspx?ID=87) pg. 77

**Prerequisites**
[vivacious speed](/Classes.aspx?ID=15)

**Requirements**
You have panache.

</column>

---

You move so quickly that you create a short-lived afterimage, looks exactly like you, in front of you or behind you. You Stride. At any point along your movement, you leave an afterimage of yourself behind. Alternatively, you can stop moving and send your afterimage forward instead, up to the remainder of your Speed. A creature that spends actions to engage with your afterimage can attempt to disbelieve it with a Will save against your class DC. Once an enemy has disbelieved any of your afterimages, they are temporarily immune to all of your Vivacious Afterimages for 10 minutes. As long as a creature has not disbelieved the afterimage, the afterimage counts as a creature for flanking. The afterimage lasts until the beginning of your next turn or until you use Vivacious Afterimage again, whichever comes first.

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Auditory" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=16" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Emotion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=60" />

<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Knights of Lastwall](/Sources.aspx?ID=123) pg. 76

**Archetype** [Knight Reclaimant](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=28)

**Prerequisites**
[Knight Reclaimant Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1097); Master in [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7)

**Requirements**
You are not [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=15).

</column>

---

Channeling the energy of the Crimson Oath into your voice, you pronounce a threat in a tone so icy it freezes the blood. Attempt an Intimidation check to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=53); you don't suffer a penalty if the target doesn't understand the language you're speaking, but this otherwise functions as normal. You can't use [Intimidating Glare](/Feats.aspx?ID=796) or any other effect that would cause your Demoralize attempt to lose the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16) trait as part of using this feat. If you critically succeed at your Intimidation check, the target becomes [stunned 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36), or stunned 2 if the target is [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160). After using this feat, you are fatigued until the end of your next turn, and you can't use this feat again until the end of your next turn.

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 21 --- You can speak with the secret tones of elements you channel, finding words in the crackle of flame, the grinding of stone. Your kinetic aura grants you these three benefits while active.
  • You can speak all the languages of your kinetic elements ([Sussuran](/Languages.aspx?ID=111) for air, [Petran](/Languages.aspx?ID=109) for earth, [Pyric](/Languages.aspx?ID=110) for fire, [Talican](/Languages.aspx?ID=112) for metal, [Thalassic](/Languages.aspx?ID=113) for water, [Muan](/Languages.aspx?ID=108) for wood).
  • You can communicate with [mindless](/Traits.aspx?ID=108) [elementals](/Traits.aspx?ID=57) on a basic level if they have a trait that matches one of your kinetic elements or are made of one of those elements. This allows you to use [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=50) on them and to make very simple [Requests](/Actions.aspx?ID=51).
  • You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Charisma-based skill checks you attempt against elementals of one of your kinetic elements.

>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Auditory" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=541" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=561" />
<trait label="Exemplar" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=839" />
<trait label="Linguistic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=642" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=647" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 35

**Prerequisites**
You are not [sanctified](/Traits.aspx?ID=519) with the [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) or [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521) trait.

</column>

---

Having seen the wreckage left by the gods and their servitors as they play in their great war of good and evil, you’ve come to the only reasonable conclusion: they all must be cut from their silken thrones. You swear a vow to defeat one creature within 60 feet that has the [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) or [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521) trait. The first time each round that you deal damage to that creature, you deal an additional 1d6 [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) damage. You can’t use Vow of Mortal Defiance again until you or the target is defeated, flees, or the encounter ends.

**Special** If you take this feat, you can’t become sanctified with the holy or unholy trait. Retraining out of this feat typically requires a major change of philosophy.

While in your trance, you can blur the line between dreams and reality for others. You gain the [_waking dream_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1198) focus spell, which you can use only while you're in a [Daydream Trance](/Feats.aspx?ID=3873). You gain a pool of Focus Points with 1 Focus Point and you can [Refocus](/Actions.aspx?ID=71) by taking a nap for 10 minutes. You become trained in occult spell attack rolls and spell DCs, and your spellcasting ability for these spells is Wisdom.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 16"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Walk on the Wind](/Feats.aspx?ID=3760) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Aftermath" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=424" />
<trait label="Air" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=5" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 57

**Prerequisites**
You've been brought to 0 Hit Points by an enemy that has the [air](/Traits.aspx?ID=5) trait or an enemy's ability that has the air trait.

</column>

---

A flighty breeze follows you wherever you go, granting a dramatic flair to everything you do. You're light on your feet, your voice gains an airy quality that allows it to travel further than normal, and your clothing and hair rustle gently around you at all times. You can Stride at half your land Speed across calm air. If you attempt to carry another creature with you while walking on air, even if it's in an [extradimensional](/Traits.aspx?ID=67) space, you fall.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Walk the Plank](/Feats.aspx?ID=2035) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 185

**Archetype** [Pirate](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=70)

**Prerequisites**
[Pirate Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2032)

</column>

---

You frighten a foe into moving where you want them, traditionally demanding they walk the plank. Attempt to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=53) an opponent; this check gains the [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93) trait. On a success, in addition to the normal effects, you can also force the target to Stride up to its Speed. You choose the path the target takes, and it does so as part of your Walk the Plank action. You can't force the target to move into a harmful space (one where it will take damage, fall, provoke reactions, or similar) unless the result of your check to Demoralize was a critical success. The target then becomes temporarily immune to Walk the Plank for 24 hours.

>
[Walk Through the Conflagration](/Feats.aspx?ID=4248) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Fire" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=72" />
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Overflow" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=506" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
<trait label="Teleportation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=156" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 29

</column>

---

You fall through your own kinetic gate, leaving behind an effigy of flame and reappearing majestically near another fire. You instantly transport yourself, and any items you're wearing and holding, from your current space to a clear space within 120 feet you can observe that's adjacent to an open flame or a creature taking [persistent fire damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29). If this would bring another creature with you—even if you're carrying it in an [extradimensional](/Traits.aspx?ID=67) container—the action fails.

 A whorl of fire surrounds you in a 5-foot emanation either before you depart or after you arrive. Each creature in the area takes 4d6 fire damage with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save against your class DC.

---
**Level (+3)** The fire damage increases by 1d6.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 7"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Wall Jump](/Feats.aspx?ID=5236) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 265

**Prerequisites**
Master in [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3)

</column>

---

You can use your momentum from a jump to propel yourself off a wall. If you’re adjacent to a wall at the end of a jump (whether performing a High Jump, Long Jump, or Leap), you don’t fall as long as your next action is another jump. Your previous jump gives you momentum, letting you use High Jump or Long Jump as a single action, but you don’t get to Stride as part of the activity.

You can use Wall Jump only once in a turn, unless you’re legendary in Athletics, in which case you can use it as many times as you can use consecutive jump actions in that turn.

<title level="2">Wall Jump leads to...</title>
[Ricocheting Leap](/Feats.aspx?ID=5708)

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

---

Roses are the symbol of Milani, and you can call forth a wall of them to stymie those who don't follow her teachings. You can cast [_wall of thorns_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1752) once per day as a 4th-rank divine innate spell. The wall is immune to fire and the piercing damage its thorns deal counts as silver for the purposes of resistances. Followers of Milani don't treat the wall's spaces as difficult terrain and don't take damage when they enter one of the wall's spaces.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Wall Run](/Feats.aspx?ID=462) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Monk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=112" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 163

**Archetype** [Ghoul](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=178) (Level 10)

</column>

---

You defy gravity, traversing vertical planes as easily as the ground. Stride up to your Speed. You must start your movement on a horizontal surface. During this movement, you can run up vertical surfaces, like walls, at your full Speed. If you end the Stride off the ground, you fall after taking your next action or when your turn ends, whichever comes first (though you can Grab an Edge, if applicable). If you have Water Step or a similar ability, Wall Run lets you run along flimsy vertical surfaces, as well as vertical liquids, such as a waterfall.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Wandering Chef Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7053) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=572" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 100

**Archetype** [Wandering Chef](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=277)

</column>

---

Whether trained in a noble kitchen or a humble home, you know how to cook delicious dishes and source ingredients from the wilderness or urban settings. You become trained in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37); if you were already trained in Crafting, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You can use [cookware](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2717) instead of an [alchemist’s toolkit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2702) to craft alchemical foods. When using the [Subsist](/Actions.aspx?ID=2368) downtime activity, you can use Crafting or Cooking [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) in place of [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49), and if you roll a failure, you get a success instead.

You gain the [Quick Alchemy](/Rules.aspx?ID=3282) benefits, but can use it only to create [consumables](/Rules.aspx?ID=2951), and the consumables must be [alchemical food](/Rules.aspx?ID=1905). Any items you choose with Alchemical Crafting must be alchemical food, but they can be 1st level or 2nd level instead of only 1st level. 

You create up to 4 [versatile vials](/Classes.aspx?ID=56) during your daily preparations. Typically, a wandering chef’s versatile vials take the form of parcels of foraged ingredients.

<title level="2">Wandering Chef Dedication leads to...</title>
[Additional Servings](/Feats.aspx?ID=7055), [Cosmic Cocktail](/Feats.aspx?ID=7059), [Feast Planner](/Feats.aspx?ID=7057), [Morning Side Dishes](/Feats.aspx?ID=7054), [Packed with Flavor](/Feats.aspx?ID=7058)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 13"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Wandering Heart](/Feats.aspx?ID=986) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Elf" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=58" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 27

**Prerequisites**
[Arctic Elf](/Heritages.aspx?ID=6), [Cavern Elf](/Heritages.aspx?ID=7), [Desert Elf](/Heritages.aspx?ID=35), [Woodland Elf](/Heritages.aspx?ID=10), or any other elf heritage based on adapting to an environment

</column>

---

While all elves adapt to their environments over time, you have traveled so widely and become attuned to so many environs that your body now changes more rapidly than other elves. After spending a week in an environment associated with an elf heritage (such as snow for arctic elf, or a forest or jungle for woodland elf) your heritage automatically changes to become that heritage. This never causes you to change to an elf heritage that isn’t related to an environment, such as [ancient elf](/Heritages.aspx?ID=34), [seer elf](/Heritages.aspx?ID=8), or [whisper elf](/Heritages.aspx?ID=9).

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[War Mage Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7976) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Class" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=397" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 68

**Archetype** [War Mage](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=331)

**Prerequisites**
You have a spellcasting class feature.

</column>

---

Your studies into the battlefield applications of magic have made your spells particularly effective at disrupting enemy  formations or manipulating enemy troops into positions where they are more vulnerable to wide-scale magical attacks. When  you cast a non-cantrip spell that deals damage in an area, choose a number of targets equal to your Intelligence modifier who failed their saving throw against the effect. Move each one up to 10 feet from their original position after they take damage and any other effects from the spell. You can't move a creature into or through obstacles. A Medium or smaller creature counts as one target; a Large creature counts as two Medium creatures; and a Huge creature counts as four Medium  creatures. You can't move Gargantuan creatures in this way.  

You also gain the [Additional Lore](/Feats.aspx?ID=5114) general feat for Warfare [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41). If you were already trained in Warfare Lore, you become trained in a Lore skill of your choice.

<title level="2">War Mage Dedication leads to...</title>
[Arcana of Iron](/Feats.aspx?ID=7980), [Intimidating Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=7981), [Mage's Field Dressing](/Feats.aspx?ID=7977), [Shield Spell Reinforcement](/Feats.aspx?ID=7978), [Shielding Formation](/Feats.aspx?ID=7982), [Siege Ritualist](/Feats.aspx?ID=7979), [Spellshield](/Feats.aspx?ID=7983)

Move each one up to 10 feet from their original position after they take damage and any other effects from the spell. You can't move a creature into or through obstacles. A Medium or smaller creature counts as one target; a Large creature counts as two Medium creatures; and a Huge creature counts as four Medium creatures. You can't move Gargantuan creatures in this way. You also gain the Additional Lore general feat for Warfare Lore. If you were already trained in Warfare Lore, you become trained in a Lore skill of your choice. War Mage Dedication leads to... Arcana of Iron, Intimidating Spell, Mage's Field Dressing, Shield Spell Reinforcement, Shielding Formation, Siege Ritualist, Spellshield

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 45

**Archetype** [Scrollmaster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=31)

**Prerequisites**
[Scrollmaster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1130)

**Trigger**
Your turn ends.

**Requirements**
You're currently affected by a [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) effect that you gained by failing, but not critically failing, a saving throw.

</column>

---

To protect the knowledge within your mind from intrusion or erasure, you ward yourself against a mental attack, temporarily delaying its effects. Until the end of your next turn, you ignore a single mental effect that meets the requirement. You can suppress a particular effect using Ward Mind or [Cognitive Loophole](/Feats.aspx?ID=593) only once, even if you have both feats.

**Special** You can use this reaction even if the mental effect prevents you from using reactions.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Warped by Rage](/Feats.aspx?ID=7179) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Exemplar" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=839" />
<trait label="Ikon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=840" />
<trait label="Morph" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=657" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 39

**Usage**
imbued into a body or worn ikon

</column>

---

Rage courses through your body, transforming you into a beast of battle. The imbued ikon gains the following abilities. 

**Immanence** You’re affected by a 4th-rank [_enlarge_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1514) spell. You can choose to forgo this effect when your body ikon becomes empowered

**Transcendence—Spasm of the Berserker** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([transcendence](/Traits.aspx?ID=842)) Your body warps beyond recognition into a powerful, one eyed form. You’re affected by a 4th-rank enlarge spell and a 6th-rank [_moon frenzy_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1609) spell, which both last until the end of your next turn. You can’t attempt to end the moon frenzy early.

If this ikon becomes empowered again, you can extend Spasm of the Berserker’s duration until the end of your next turn. While you’re already affected by Spasm of the Berserker, the transcend action becomes a free action to extend its duration until the end of your next turn.

    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Restricted"
>
[Warped Constriction](/Feats.aspx?ID=3820) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 141

**Archetype** [Living Vessel](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=188)

**Prerequisites**
[Living Vessel Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3815); your entity is an [aberration](/Traits.aspx?ID=1) or outer entity

**Requirements**
You have a foe [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=33).

</column>

---

The entity inhabiting your body is an aberrant being with unfathomable motivations, and when you hold a foe close, tendrils and tentacles unfurl from your body to crush your foe and pollute it with alien wrongness. Your grabbed or restrained foe takes bludgeoning damage equal to your level and mental damage equal to your highest mental ability modifier. The creature attempts a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Will save that applies to both types of damage and uses the higher of your class DC or spell DC.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Emotion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=60" />
<trait label="Fear" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=68" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=106" />
<trait label="Reflection" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=431" />
<trait label="Visual" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=163" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 120

**Frequency**
once per minute

</column>

---

Due to your origins, your form is more flexible than most. You shift your appearance to resemble a creature within 30 feet but with an unsettling, horrifying twist. Though this transformation is momentary, witnessing it gives the target deep existential dread. It must succeed at a Will save against the higher of your class DC or spell DC or become [frightened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19) (frightened 2 on a critical failure) and be stupefied 1 as long as the frightened condition lasts. Once you've used Warped Reflection against a creature, it's temporarily immune for 24 hours.

You have been given a powerful blessing of battle that is also your cursed doom. As long as you aren’t wearing heavy armor or wielding a [shield](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=12), [spears](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=14) and [polearms](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=11) you wield gain the [parry](/Traits.aspx?ID=667) trait. If the weapon already has the parry trait, increase the bonus when parrying to +2. In addition, you deal an additional amount of damage equal to your [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67) value with weapons in the spear and polearm groups. This damage is the same type as the required weapon.

**Prerequisites**

---

When you choose a warshard weapon during your daily preparations, you can empower it with an additional magical effect. Choose one common weapon [property rune](/Rules.aspx?ID=3168) that’s of a level equal to or lower than your level. That rune is applied to your warshard weapon as if it were etched onto it normally, but this weapon property does not count against the normal maximum number of property runes a weapon can have. If you empower a weapon with a property rune of the same type, only the highest-level one applies. This additional rune functions only when you wield your warshard weapon and have at least 1 unspent Mythic Point; otherwise, the rune becomes dormant until these conditions are met.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs=""
>
[Warshard Warrior Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8178) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Revenge of the Runelords</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Destiny" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=838" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star](/Sources.aspx?ID=283) pg. 84

**Archetype** [Warshard Warrior](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=341)

</column>

---

When you became infused with a shard of the god of war, you knew in your gut that your destiny would be one for the ages—yet you may not, at first, know the exact way such a destiny would play out. If you still carry the warshard that empowered you, you might carry it as a token or wear it as jewelry—if indeed it’s not simply embedded into your body. Regardless, the warshard itself no longer has any intrinsic power of its own, and even if you toss the warshard aside, its gifts do not leave you, nor can another benefit from them. If you throw the warshard away or lose it, your destiny remains unaltered; you have, in effect, become the warshard itself. This power manifests through a weapon you wield.

When you make your daily preparations, choose one weapon in your possession in which you have at least expert proficiency. That weapon becomes your warshard weapon until you choose a different weapon in your possession during another of your daily preparations. You can choose a mundane nonmagical weapon, a weapon with magical runes, one made of an unusual material, or even a specific magic weapon such as a [storm flash](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2873) or a [bloodletting kukri](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2862), but not an intelligent weapon or an artifact like the bastard sword [Serithtial](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3123) or one of the seven swords of sin. While you don’t lose access to your warshard warrior feats if your warshard weapon is taken from you or destroyed, note that several of this destiny’s feats require you to be wielding your warshard weapon. You can etch or remove runes from a warshard weapon normally. You can have only one warshard weapon at a time.

Your gain the [Mythic Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=7302) feat, but you can only use it with your warshard weapon.

Whenever you make a Strike with your warshard weapon at mythic proficiency, you double the amount of additional damage you deal with the weapon specialization class feature. When you make Crafting checks to Repair your warshard weapon, your treat your proficiency rank in Crafting as legendary for determining how many Hit Points you restore to the item; in addition, if your Crafting result is a critical failure, you get a failure instead.

You also gain the following action. 

<document level="2" id="action-3534" />

<title level="2">Warshard Warrior Dedication leads to...</title>
[Athlete's Ally](/Feats.aspx?ID=8179), [Divide and Conquer](/Feats.aspx?ID=8184), [Final Shot Knows the Way](/Feats.aspx?ID=8187), [I Am the Weapon](/Feats.aspx?ID=8189), [Indomitable Shot](/Feats.aspx?ID=8185), [Lightless Sight](/Feats.aspx?ID=8180), [Prescient Parry](/Feats.aspx?ID=8186), [Steadfast Grip](/Feats.aspx?ID=8181), [Throw and Catch](/Feats.aspx?ID=8188), [Transmute Weapon](/Feats.aspx?ID=8182), [Warshard Rune](/Feats.aspx?ID=8183)

Pathfinder agents serve as members of diverse teams with complementary skill sets. You are practiced at following the example of a more skilled ally to accomplish a wide variety of tasks. For the next minute you can add your level as a proficiency bonus to the observed skill check, even though you are untrained. This does not allow you to attempt trained actions using that skill unless you would otherwise be able to do so.

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

---

You pay close attention to the people around you, allowing you to more easily notice when they act out of character. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks when using the [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=85) basic action to notice enchanted or possessed characters. If you aren't actively using Sense Motive on an enchanted or possessed character, the GM rolls a secret check, without your usual circumstance bonus, for you to potentially notice the enchantment or possession anyway.

In addition to using it for skill checks, you can use the [Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=75) basic action to grant a bonus to another creature's saving throw or other check to overcome enchantment or possession. As usual for Aid, you need to prepare by using an action on your turn to encourage the creature to fight against the effect.

Master in [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3)

</column>

---

Experience and training have taught you that water has just enough surface tension for a master sprinter to traverse the surface. When you Stride in a straight line, if you move at least half your Speed over ground, you can move any amount of the remaining distance across a level body of water. If you don't end your Stride on solid ground, you fall into the water. 

If you're legendary in [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3), as long as you start on solid ground, any part of your Stride can cross the water's surface, even if you aren't moving a straight line, though you still fall into the water if you don't end your movement on solid ground.

You allow your body to collapse into water, then reconstitute your corporeal form elsewhere. You can cast [_translocate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1724) as an [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662) innate spell twice per day; the spell additionally gains the [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=732) trait. If you [Cast this Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) while standing in a body of water of at least ankle depth, you don’t need to perform any incantations or gestures to Cast the Spell (typically preventing reactions, such as [Reactive Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2256)), and the spell gains the [subtle](/Traits.aspx?ID=522) trait as you simply fall into the water without so much as a splash.

---

In your hands, swords dance like rainfall over the waves; who can tell where the storm ends and the sea begins? Developed by Swordmaster Ganhil to compete with the House of Untwisting Iron, this stance integrates fluid swordplay into even the simplest movements.

 While in Waterfowl Stance, the dandpatta, scimitar, talwar, and zulfikar gain the monk trait for you. When you [Tumble Through](/Actions.aspx?ID=2370) a creature’s space or [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=2298) over a creature while wielding one of these weapons, you can deal that creature 1d6 slashing damage. This damage is increased to 2d6 if the weapon has a _[greater striking rune](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829)_ and 3d6 if it has a _[major striking rune](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829)._

**Special** You gain access to the [dandpatta](/Weapons.aspx?ID=260), [talwar](/Weapons.aspx?ID=266), and [zulfikar](/Weapons.aspx?ID=269)

Water is the source of life, and you draw upon this primordial force to heal your allies' wounds. You learned to fight with weapons that help you keep your distance or make the most of striking from shadows. You can use the unusual resonance of your [_wayfinder_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=470) to grant it additional effects. Choose one cantrip from the [arcane](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=1), [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2), [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3), or [primal](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=4) list. Additionally, you can Activate your [_wayfinder_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=470) with a <actions string="Single Action" /> (envision) activation to transform it into a nondescript pin or brooch to hide your affiliation with the Pathfinder Society. This transformation lasts for 1 hour.

You and your [companion](/Traits.aspx?ID=558) move as one, never tripping each other up. This fluid movement throws your enemies off balance. You and your united companion can share each other’s spaces. When you do so, both you and your united companion provide [lesser cover](/Rules.aspx?ID=2372) to one another. You and your united companion also count as being adjacent to one another when sharing each other’s spaces. A target is automatically [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) against the first [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) each round each of you and your united companion make while sharing one another’s spaces; this benefit also applies if you are [mounted](/Traits.aspx?ID=411) on your united companion.

**Access**
Members of the Firebrands at the rank of second mark or higher have access to this feat.

**Trigger**
An ally you can see and hear is about to attempt a [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) check to [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46) someone or [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=47).

---

Emulating Shensen whenever she arrives at a show, you share your knowledge of the region and drop a few important local names to make a good impression and help your allies do the same. Attempt a [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) check to [Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=75) your ally. If you succeed, you recall a few specific details about local culture and personalities to help support your ally's deception. In addition to the benefits of your Aid, the triggering ally rolls their Deception check twice and takes the better result. This is a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=76) effect.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Weapon-Rune Shifter](/Feats.aspx?ID=1150) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #148: Fires of the Haunted City](/Sources.aspx?ID=13) pg. 75

**Archetype** [Crystal Keeper](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=34)

**Prerequisites**
[Crystal Keeper Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1146)

</column>

---

You learn how to alter the magic of weapon runes by using a crystal as a focusing component. Once per day during your daily preparations, you can focus on a rune’s magical energies through a crystal’s facets to alter a single property rune on one weapon in your possession to suppress its normal effects and make it function as a different property rune. You can temporarily alter the rune to function as one of the following runes: [_corrosive_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=292), [_flaming_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=295), [_frost_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=296), [_ghost touch_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=297), [_grievous_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=298), [_returning_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=301), [_shock_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=303), [_thundering_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=306), or [_wounding_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=309). The property rune remains altered until you make your next daily preparations. The weapon must meet the prerequisites for the temporary rune, and any other runes that required the suppressed rune are also suppressed while the rune is transformed. The rune is obviously altered, and thus the weapon can’t be sold as though it had the temporary rune.

**Archetype** [Swarmkeeper](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=223)

**Prerequisites**

**Requirements**
Your swarm is outside your body.

</column>

---

Your swarm can spin dense webs much like those left by stone-gray weaver spiders under eaves and in derelict city buildings, especially along the coasts of Varisia. When your swarm ends its turn, it fills all surfaces in its space with sticky webs that last for 1 minute. The webs are [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453). A creature that ends its turn in the webs must succeed at a Reflex save or be [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81) until it [Escapes](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296). The webs' save DC and Escape DC are equal to the higher of your class DC or spell DC. The swarm is immune to its webs.

</title>

</traits>

</column>

---

You can produce a soft silk to weave into useful items. You gain the [Specialty Crafting](/Feats.aspx?ID=844) feat with a specialty in weaving. You can use your webbing to [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=43) simple, nonconsumable threaded items, such as clothing and rope, at zero cost as long as their base Price is 1 sp or less. These items have no resale value, and they naturally degrade after 24 hours without regular (if minor) maintenance. You can maintain up to 10 such items at a time; if you create a new one, your oldest creation breaks down from neglect. These temporary items take you only 1 day to Craft instead of 4. If you're an expert in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4), you can Craft these items in 1 hour; if you're a master, you can Craft them in 10 minutes; if you're legendary, you can Craft them in 1 minute.

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 76 **Archetype** [Werecreature](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=225) **Requirements** You were born into a lineage of true werecreatures or were afflicted with the curse of the werecreature. --- You're a werecreature, able to shift between your humanoid shape, an animal shape, and a monstrous hybrid of the two. You gain the beast and werecreature traits. Choose your werecreature type from the table below. Once chosen, this can't be changed. You gain the [Toughness](/Feats.aspx?ID=5227) feat but also a weakness to [silver](/Equipment.aspx?ID=379) equal to half your level. You gain the Change Shape action. >
[Westyr's Wayfinder Repository](/Feats.aspx?ID=2273) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 119

**Archetype** [Pathfinder Agent](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=13)

**Prerequisites**
[Pathfinder Agent Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=871); [Wayfinder Resonance Tinkerer](/Feats.aspx?ID=875)

**Requirements**
You have at least one 1st-level spell slot and a [_wayfinder_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=470).

</column>

---

You can use your _wayfinder_ to store a little extra magic for when you need it most. When making your daily preparations, you can choose one 1st-level spell from your spellbook or spell repertoire and store it in your _wayfinder_. You can cast this spell from the _wayfinder_ using the normal actions required. Once the spell has been cast, it is expended, and you must make your next daily preparations to store another spell in your _wayfinder_.

<title level="2">Spells Training</title>

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 119

Sorrina Westyr (_Lost Omens Pathfinder Society Guide_ page 46) took up the mantle of dean of the school of Spells to replace her predecessor Aram Zey, who had originally been her replacement. When Aram Zey was lost to the magic of the extradimensional demiplane known as the Hao Jin Tapestry, Sorrina began teaching an advanced studies course in extradimensional and interplanar phenomena, hoping to both prevent future losses and better prepare her students for the unexpected challenges that may await them in their careers as Pathfinder agents.

**Related Feats**:

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 185

**Archetype** [Time Mage](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=191)

**Prerequisites**
[Time Mage Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3839)

</column>

---

Rather than conjuring creatures from elsewhere in the world or the planes, you can temporarily pull a much different version of yourself from an alternate timeline—for instance, instead of summoning a generic or random [troll](/Monsters.aspx?ID=395) with [_summon giant_](/Spells.aspx?ID=324), you summon a troll version of yourself from a timeline where you're a troll. If your next action is to Cast a Spell that summons a creature, that creature is another version of you. This creature remains the type of creature you summoned and has largely the same abilities (plus the following adjustments), but it clearly resembles you, likely sharing some distinguishing features, such as mannerisms, speech patterns, tattoos, or clothing. The summoned creature gains a +1 status bonus to any skill check in which you're trained, a +2 status bonus if you're an expert, a +3 status bonus if you're a master, or a +4 status bonus if you're legendary. The creature also takes a –2 penalty to all skills in which you're untrained.

Whether as a dealer or player, you've learned to spot cheaters. When another creature attempts to [Conceal an Object](/Actions.aspx?ID=61) from you, use your Gambling Lore DC if it's higher than your Perception DC to determine whether they succeed.     level="1"
    right="Feat 14"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Whirling Blade Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=1755) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Monk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=112" />
<trait label="Stance" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=152" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 130

**Prerequisites**
[Monastic Weaponry](/Feats.aspx?ID=434)

</column>

---

You enter a mindful stance that creates a deep connection between you and your monk weapons, allowing you to manipulate them with your ki even at a distance. All melee monk weapons you wield with the [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179) trait gain the [thrown](/Traits.aspx?ID=195) 10 feet trait (unless they already have the thrown trait with a greater range).

 Once you've made a thrown Strike with such a weapon, you can use the precision of your throw to make additional strikes with it, even from a distance. Start from the space of the previous Strike's target to determine the range increment and whether the new target has cover. At the end of your turn, the thrown weapon flies directly back to you in a straight line. If a solid barrier blocks its path, it falls to the ground after hitting the barrier.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 16"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Whirling Clobber](/Feats.aspx?ID=5485) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Attack" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=540" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 75

**Archetype** [Thlipit Contestant](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=224)

**Prerequisites**
[Thlipit Contestant Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=5474)

**Requirements**
You have a creature [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90) with your lash.

</column>

---

After you've grasped a creature with your lash, you swing them around like a whirling hammer, smashing them into all nearby enemies. Make a melee Strike against each enemy within your melee reach. Your last attack must be against the grabbed creature, and you gain a circumstance bonus to your attack roll equal to the number of enemies you slammed them into, to a maximum of +3. Each attack counts toward your multiple attack penalty, but don't increase your penalty until you have made all your attacks. After your Whirling Clobber, you release the grabbed or restrained creature into an open square within reach of your lash.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Whirling Grindstone](/Feats.aspx?ID=4300) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Attack" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=15" />
<trait label="Composite" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=501" />
<trait label="Earth" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=55" />
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Metal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=505" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 36

</column>

---

A whirling grindstone made of flint appears in an unoccupied square within 30 feet. The grindstone shreds flesh and shoots sparks. Attempt an impulse attack roll against the AC of a creature adjacent to the grindstone. On a hit, the creature takes 2d6 slashing damage and 1d6 fire damage (or double damage on a critical hit). The grindstone lasts until the end of your next turn, and you can Sustain the impulse up to 1 minute. On subsequent turns, the first time you Sustain the impulse that turn, you can roll the grindstone up to 20 feet and can repeat the attack.

 A creature within reach of the grindstone can Interact with it to sharpen a metal weapon. This grants a +2 circumstance bonus to the next damage roll made with that weapon within 1 minute.

---
**Level (+5)** The grindstone's damage increases by 1d6 slashing and 1d6 fire, and the bonus to weapons increases by 1.

</title>

<trait label="Monk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=656" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

Your hands move in a hypnotic and distracting flurry that throws your foes off-balance before you cast them away with a violent pirouette. You [Step](/Actions.aspx?ID=2304). Then each enemy within your reach must attempt a Will save against the higher of your class DC or your Deception DC; on a failure, they’re [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) to melee attacks from you and your allies until the end of your next turn. Then, [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=2380) up to three adjacent enemies; each Shove counts toward your multiple attack penalty, but you don’t increase your penalty until after you’ve resolved all the Shove attempts.

Then each enemy within your reach must attempt a Will save against the higher of your class DC or your Deception DC; on a failure, they’re off-guard to melee attacks from you and your allies until the end of your next turn. Then, Shove up to three adjacent enemies; each Shove counts toward your multiple attack penalty, but you don’t increase your penalty until after you’ve resolved all the Shove attempts.

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 136 **Archetype** [Pistol Phenom](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=120) **Prerequisites** [Pistol Phenom Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3251) **Requirements** You're wielding a loaded one-handed firearm and a one-handed melee weapon. --- You fire your gun while throwing off a target's balance with your melee weapon. Then, you topple your foe to the ground with the quick orchestrated combination. You don't need to use brute force to do so, or even necessarily to hit with your gunshot; the effect is all about performing perfectly and eliminating your target's movements and options, leaving them no choice but to fall. Make a ranged firearm Strike against a creature within the reach of your melee weapon and then attempt a [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) check against the creature's Reflex DC. If the Strike critically succeeds, the target takes a –2 circumstance penalty to its Reflex DC against this check. The Performance check has the following effects. **Critical Success** The target falls and lands [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31). It takes 2d6 bludgeoning damage from the fall.
**Success** The target falls and lands prone.
**Critical Failure** Your plans backfired on you, and you're forced to drop your melee weapon in your space.

You can throw the creature any distance up to 10 feet, plus 5 feet × your Strength modifier. If you successfully throw the creature, it takes bludgeoning damage equal to your Strength modifier plus 1d6 per 10 feet you threw it. Attempt an Athletics check against the foe’s Fortitude DC. You take a –2 circumstance penalty to your check if the target is one size larger than you and a –4 circumstance penalty if it’s larger than that. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your check if the target is one size smaller than you and a +4 circumstance bonus if it’s smaller than that. **Critical Success** You throw the creature the desired distance and it lands prone.
**Success** You throw the creature the desired distance.
**Failure** You don’t throw the creature.
**Critical Failure** You don’t throw the creature, and it’s no longer grabbed or restrained by you.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 20"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Whirlwind Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=2885) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=389" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 49

**Prerequisites**
[Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=755)

**Requirements**
Your Spellstrike is charged.

</column>

---

You combine the might of a multitarget spell with a whirling flurry of attacks. You use Spellstrike, making a melee Strike against each enemy within your reach instead of against one enemy. If your spell can affect multiple targets, your spell affects all foes you hit, not just the first target, up to the spell's normal maximum targets. If you Strike more foes than the spell could target, choose which foes are affected by the spell. Each attack counts toward your multiple attack penalty but doesn't increase your penalty until you've made all your attacks.

 If you use [Expansive Spellstrike](/Feats.aspx?ID=2849) to Spellstrike with an area spell, apply the area as described in Expansive Spellstrike, choosing one of the creatures you Strike to determine the area and whether the spell fails due to a critically failed Strike. If you use Expansive Spellstrike to Spellstrike with a targeted spell, each creature you critically fail to Strike is unaffected by the spell, but the spell isn't lost completely from a single critical failure. You can use this activity with only melee Strikes, even if you have the [starlit span](/HybridStudies.aspx?ID=4) hybrid study or a similar ability.

You whirl a foe to smash into all nearby creatures before throwing them far away in imitation of the techniques of your rival, Ran-To. You [Thrash](/Feats.aspx?ID=156). You speak in a whisper, a soft wind carrying your words far away. This has the effect of the [_message_](/Spells.aspx?ID=190) spell with a range of 500 feet, and it can target only a creature surrounded by air. <traits>

<trait label="Psychic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=430" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 27

</column>

---

Your spell leaves a lingering connection between you and a creature—one through which you can nudge the creature's mind this way or that. The amped cantrip must take 2 or more actions to cast, target one or more creatures, and either require a spell attack roll or have a saving throw. Use this amp in place of the psi cantrip's normal amp entry.

---
**Amp** Choose one enemy who is a target of the spell. If that enemy fails its save or the spell hits it, you whisper in the creature's mind, forcing it to Step in a direction of your choosing; as this is [forced movement](/Rules.aspx?ID=451), you can't force the creature to Step into hazardous terrain, off a ledge, or the like. After it Steps, the creature becomes temporarily immune to this amp for 24 hours.

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 63 **Frequency** once per day --- You carefully consider your case and narrow down some of the details. When you [Pursue a Lead](/Actions.aspx?ID=544), you can spend 10 minutes instead of 1 minute to ask two questions of the GM as you complete the activity. The GM must answer truthfully with “yes” or “no,” though if the answer would be misleading or have no practical application to your investigation the GM can answer “immaterial.” You can't use Who Dunnit? more than once for the same lead, even across different days. Your questions must come from the following list, applying to either the creature or the clue you found:
  • Was the clue left by a [creature trait]? (Choose a creature trait such as [humanoid](/Traits.aspx?ID=91), [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160), or [dwarf](/Traits.aspx?ID=54); this trait must be accurate as of the time the clue was left.)
  • Was this clue left within the last hour?
  • Was this clue left within the last day?
  • Was the creature that left the clue in a heightened emotional state when it left the clue?
  • Did the creature attempt to conceal this clue?

You manipulate the energy of your spell, causing it to spread out and affect a wider area. If the next action you use is to Cast a Spell that has an area of a burst, cone, or line and does not have a duration, increase the area of that spell. Add 5 feet to the radius of a burst that normally has a radius of at least 10 feet (a burst with a smaller radius is not affected). Add 5 feet to the length of a cone or line that is normally 15 feet long or smaller, and add 10 feet to the length of a larger cone or line.

</column>

---

When you cast _dancing lights_, you can modify its duration to be 1 minute and modify its standard effects to create a single floating light in the shape of a Tiny creature, instead of up to four floating lights. The creature hovers over your head unless you spend a single action that has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait to direct the light to move up to 30 feet, in which case it remains there until you direct it again. If you direct it back to your head, it hovers there and follows you again until you direct it elsewhere. If the light ever moves beyond 120 feet of you, it winks out immediately.

---

Fighting in the wilds has honed your understanding of the unique abilities many creatures have. You're trained in [Wild Mimic Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41), a special Lore skill that can be used only to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) about creatures to learn their abilities. If you have legendary proficiency in Nature, you gain expert proficiency in Wild Mimic Lore, but you can't increase your proficiency in Wild Mimic Lore by any other means. When you succeed at a Wild Mimic Lore to Recall Knowledge, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your saving throws against the next attack or ability that the subject of your Recall Knowledge targets you with.

**Source** [The Fall of Plaguestone](/Sources.aspx?ID=3) pg. 57

**Prerequisites**

</column>

---

Select one type of terrain from the following list: aquatic, arctic, desert, forest, mountain, plains, sky, swamp, or underground. You can use [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) in place of Perception to roll initiative when in the selected terrain in a natural location (not a structure) even if you weren’t tracking or otherwise using [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) before the encounter. You can also use [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) instead of Perception to notice traps in natural locations in the chosen terrain; if you find a snare in this way, you can also use [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) instead of [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) to Disable the Device.

**Special** You can select this feat more than once. Each time you select it, the feat applies to a new type of terrain.

<title level="2">Noala's Training</title>

**Source** [The Fall of Plaguestone](/Sources.aspx?ID=3) pg. 56

By aiding an NPC from The Fall of Plaguestone, the PCs can learn some special woodland survival techniques.

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 25 --- Speaking lies, you set them loose upon a drifting wind. You create an auditory illusion that comes from a square within 500 feet and can be as loud as four normal humans talking. The sound can be intricate, including speech or music, though the GM might require you to attempt a check or know a language for it to be convincing. The illusion lasts until the end of your next turn, and you can Sustain the impulse. You can have any creature within 40 feet of the illusion, or that comes within 40 feet of it during the duration, attempt a Will save against your class DC. This is a [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) effect. **Success** The creature is unaffected, disbelieves the illusion, and is temporarily immune for 1 hour.
**Failure** The creature is [fascinated](/Conditions.aspx?ID=14) with the source of the sound until the end of its next turn. When the fascination ends, the creature is temporarily immune for 1 hour.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the creature is fascinated for 1 minute or until it [disbelieves](/Monsters.aspx?ID=267).

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Willing Death](/Feats.aspx?ID=2358) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Duskwalker" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=257" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Ancestry Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=74) pg. 30

**Frequency**
once per day

**Trigger**
An ally within 30 feet takes damage that would otherwise reduce them to 0 Hit Points and give them the [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=11) condition.

</column>

---

Once, you died because you valued someone else's life above your own; just as then, you protect an ally by suffering in their stead. Reduce the damage the triggering ally would take by 1 + your level. You redirect this damage to yourself, but your immunities, weaknesses, resistances, and so on don't apply. You aren't subject to any conditions or other effects from whatever damaged your ally (such as poison from a venomous bite)—your ally is still subject to those effects even if you redirect all of the triggering damage to yourself. If the redirected damage prevents the ally from being reduced to 0 Hit Points, they remain conscious and don't gain the dying condition.

**Special** You can select this feat only at 1st level, and you can't retrain into or out of this feat.

[Wind Pillow](/Feats.aspx?ID=3933) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Sylph" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=311" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Lands](/Sources.aspx?ID=146) pg. 31

</column>

---

The winds have whispered to you all your life, and the essence of air itself helps you at times, making you somewhat buoyant when you're suspended in space. Treat all [falls](/Rules.aspx?ID=402) as though they were 10 feet less than the actual distance traveled. You also gain the [Powerful Leap](/Feats.aspx?ID=820) skill feat, even if you don't meet that feat's prerequisites.

</title>

<traits>

---

Wings free you from the shackles of the ground below. You add [_aerial form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1437) to your apparition spell repertoire, allowing you to cast it with your apparition spellcasting. Whenever you use _aerial form_ to gain a form that grants you a specific [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) modifier, you gain a +1 status bonus to Acrobatics checks.

**Special** If you are attuned to an apparition of darkened boughs, add the bat and bird forms in aerial form to your [_darkened forest form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=2143) lists.

<title

    right="Feat 8"
    pfs=""
>
[Windborne Shove](/Feats.aspx?ID=8023) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Myth-Speaker</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #218: Titanbane
](/Sources.aspx?ID=274) pg. 69

**Prerequisites**
[guardian's calling](/MythicCallings.aspx?ID=6)

</column>

---

The hero-god of phalanxes and winds, grand Konebrys, led a force of dozens against an army of thousands. They gathered their soldiers in tight ranks, then marched against the wind to take the enemy by surprise. When a gust pushed the foes back, they struck their victorious blow. 

You emulate Konebrys’s tactics in pushing small forces against mighty foes. Whenever you are adjacent to an ally, creatures that attempt to [Tumble Through](/Actions.aspx?ID=2370) your space take a –2 circumstance penalty to their [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) check.

When you critically succeed on a melee Strike against an enemy, you can immediately attempt to [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=2380) your target as a free action. You can spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3323) on this Shove attempt to do so at [mythic proficiency](/Rules.aspx?ID=3322).

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />

You rush forward, flapping your wings for a bit of lift, and can use that momentum to knock down a foe. [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=2298), and if you land within melee reach of at least one enemy, you can attempt to [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=2382) that enemy. You don't need to have one hand free. If you successfully knock the target [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88), you can Leap again. If you have a fly Speed, you can [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312) instead of Leap.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Wing Shove](/Feats.aspx?ID=5534) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 83

**Archetype** [Winged Warrior](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=227)

**Prerequisites**
[Winged Warrior Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=5527)

**Requirements**
You’re flanked by at least two enemies

</column>

---

You spread your wings wide, pushing foes away from you. Attempt to [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=2380) one of the flanking enemies, and then make a second Shove attempt against a different enemy that is flanking you. You don't need one hand free. The second Shove attempt has the same multiple attack penalty as the first and doesn't count toward your multiple attack penalty. On a success or critical success, you can't Stride after a target, but that target is also [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the beginning of their next turn. While drakes and dragons are able flyers, they’re uncomfortable carrying a rider in the air without special training. Through hard work, nerves of steel, and the deep bond you share with your draconic companion, your companion has learned to carry you skyward, if only briefly. Your dragon companion gains the Winged Leap action. 

**Winged Leap** <actions string="Single Action" /> **Frequency** once per round; **Effect** Your dragon companion [Flies](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312). If it doesn’t normally have a [fly Speed](/Rules.aspx?ID=2350), it gains a fly Speed of 25 feet for this movement. If it isn’t on solid ground at the end of this movement, it falls.

You're among the few kobolds who grow a set of draconic wings later in life. The wings are initially small and weak; while not enough for full flight, a strong flap allows you to jump further. When [Leaping](/Actions.aspx?ID=81) horizontally, you move an additional 5 feet (this additional distance isn't cumulative with the increased Leap distance from the [Powerful Leap](/Feats.aspx?ID=820) feat). You don't automatically fail your checks to [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=36) or [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=37) if you don't Stride at least 10 feet first. In addition, when you attempt a Long Jump, you can jump a distance up to 10 feet longer than you normally would based on the result of your [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check, though you still can't jump farther than your Speed.

Bone-chilling, swirling sleet surrounds you, cruel as deepest winter. Surfaces in your kinetic aura are coated in slippery ice. A creature that moves on the ice immediately falls unless it succeeds at an Acrobatics check or Reflex save against your impulse DC – 2. A creature that Steps or Crawls doesn’t have to attempt a check or save. You’re immune to this effect.

 If a creature on the ice is critically hit by one of your water [impulses](/Traits.aspx?ID=502) or critically fails at a save against one, that creature is [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) until the end of its next turn.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 20"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Wish Alchemy](/Feats.aspx?ID=2159) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Alchemist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=7" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Legends](/Sources.aspx?ID=40) pg. 20

</column>

---

You have learned Artokus Kirran's most hidden secrets, granting you the ability to create alchemy infused with the power of wishes. Once per day when you use advanced alchemy during your daily preparations, you can spend a batch of infused reagents to create a wish vial containing a single common [arcane](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=1) spell of your choice of 8th level or lower. The spell must have a casting time of no more than 3 actions, no Cost, and must be able to target you. Only you can Activate the wish vial, which takes the same number of Interact actions as the spell's casting time and grants you the effects of the spell.

<title level="2">Artokus's Discoveries</title>

**Source** [Legends](/Sources.aspx?ID=40) pg. 20

Artokus Kirran's legacy includes far more than just the sun orchid elixir. As one of the longest-lived alchemists in Golarion, he's developed a number of other significant alchemical discoveries known across the Inner Sea region. The following are some of his more notable discoveries. Artokus is cautious about sharing his alchemical techniques and typically only does so with his most trusted students.

**Related Feats**: [Artokus's Fire](/Feats.aspx?ID=2158)

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 154

**Archetype** [Witch](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=44)

**Prerequisites**
Intelligence 14

</column>

---

You cast spells like a witch. Choose a [patron](/Patrons.aspx); you gain a [familiar](/Familiars.aspx) with two common cantrips of your choice from your chosen patron's tradition, but aside from the tradition, you don't gain any other effects the patron would usually grant. Your familiar has one less familiar ability than normal. You gain the Cast a Spell activity. You can prepare one cantrip each day from your familiar. You're trained in spell attack rolls and spell DCs from your patron's tradition. Your key spellcasting ability for witch archetype spells is Intelligence, and they are witch spells of your patron's tradition. You become trained in the skill associated with the patron's tradition; if you were already trained in it, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the witch archetype.

<title level="2">Witch Dedication leads to...</title>

</column>

---

You cast spells like a witch. Choose a patron; you gain a [familiar](/Rules.aspx?ID=2121) with two common cantrips of your choice from your chosen patron's tradition, but aside from the tradition, you don't gain any other effects the patron would usually grant. Your familiar gains the normal number of abilities for a familiar instead of those a witch familiar normally gets. 

You gain the [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) activity. You can prepare one cantrip each day from your familiar. You're trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. Your key spellcasting attribute for witch archetype spells is Intelligence, and they are witch spells of your patron's tradition. You become trained in the skill associated with the patron's tradition; if you were already trained in it, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice

[Witch Warden](/Feats.aspx?ID=949) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Human" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=90" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 13

**Access**
Kellid ethnicity

</column>

---

You and your family have fought long and hard against witches, particularly the winter witches of Irrisen, and you've learned to be wary of their curses and the otherworldly powers their patrons grant. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against [curses](/Traits.aspx?ID=38), and to saving throws against spells cast by a [witch](/Classes.aspx?ID=16) or [hag](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=59). If you roll a success on a saving throw against a curse or a spell cast by a witch or hag, you get a critical success instead.

  • **Eldritch Nails** Your nails are supernaturally long and sharp. You gain a nails unarmed attack that deals 1d6 slashing damage, is in the brawling group, and has the agile and unarmed traits.
  • **Iron Teeth** With a click of your jaw, your teeth transform into long metallic points. You gain a jaws unarmed attack that deals 1d8 piercing damage and is in the brawling group.
  • **Living Hair** You can instantly grow or shrink your hair, eyebrows, beard, or mustache by up to several feet and manipulate your hair for use as a weapon, though your control isn’t fine enough for more dexterous tasks. You gain a hair unarmed attack that deals 1d4 bludgeoning damage; is in the brawling group; and has the agile, disarm, finesse, trip, and unarmed traits.
**Special** You can take this feat more than once, gaining a different unarmed attack each time. Witch's Armaments leads to... [Sympathetic Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=5000), [Wild Witch's Armaments](/Feats.aspx?ID=5414)

    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Witch's Bottle](/Feats.aspx?ID=1578) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Witch" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=323" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 103

**Prerequisites**
[Cauldron](/Feats.aspx?ID=1562)

</column>

---

You spend 10 minutes and 1 Focus Point brewing a special potion containing the power of one of your hexes that targets a creature. A creature that consumes this potion is targeted by the hex. If the hex has a sustained duration and you have [_cackle_](/Spells.aspx?ID=792), you can cast _cackle_ into the bottle just before you seal it. If you do, the hex's duration is extended as if you had cast _cackle_ the round after the hex was cast (typically this extends the duration by 1 round). Your cackling laugh sounds out when the potion is unsealed.

 Any potion you create this way loses its power the next time you make your daily preparations. While the potion is in your possession, you can render it inert using a single action that has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait. You can't regain the Focus Point you spent to create the potion (or the Focus Point you spent to cast _cackle_) until the potion is consumed or loses its magic.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Witch’s Broom](/Feats.aspx?ID=5014) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Witch" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=734" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 190

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Crafting a witch's broomstick into a flying broomstick must be done by the witch with the Witch's Broom feat themself, not another crafter._

</column>

---

A broom is the only steed you need to fly through the night sky. During your daily preparations, you can anoint a single broom, staff, polearm, or similarly shaped object with a flying ointment made of special herbs and oils. Until the next time you make your daily preparations, it gains the magical trait, and you can ride on it while you’re holding it with at least 1 hand. It moves at a fly Speed of 20 feet. The broom takes a –10-foot penalty to its Speed if laden with more than 20 Bulk, and crashes to the ground if it carries more than 30 Bulk. The broom can’t be controlled by anyone but you. If you anoint a weapon or other held item, you can’t ride the broom and wield it at the same time.

You can Craft your broomstick into a [_flying broomstick_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3023)
as though you had the formula for that item. If you anoint an item that’s already a flying broomstick, the broom gains a +10-foot status bonus to its Speed and you can choose whether it works for anyone or only you.

[Witch's Charge](/Feats.aspx?ID=1575) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Detection" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=43" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Witch" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=323" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 102

</column>

---

You forge a magical link with another creature, granting you awareness of that creature's condition and creating a conduit for spellcasting. During your daily preparations, you can designate one willing creature as your charge. You are always aware of your charge's direction from you, its distance from you, and any conditions affecting it. In addition, you can cast spells with a range of touch on your charge from a range of 30 feet. These effects persist until your next daily preparations.

**Special** This feat has the trait corresponding to the tradition of spells you cast ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120), or [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)).
