**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 105 --- Your home is an animated structure that obeys your commands. By performing a rite that takes 1 day, you create an animated object from a hut, small house, covered wagon, tent, or similar construction of up to Huge size. The hut uses your AC, saving throw modifiers, and Perception modifier and has 150 HP and Hardness 10. It has the construct armor ability, meaning once it's reduced to less than half its Hit Points, or immediately upon being damaged by a critical hit, its AC is reduced by 4 until it is repaired. The hut can't attack or attempt skill checks. You can give the hut a command as a single action, which has the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16) and [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) traits; after 1 round of reconfiguring itself, the hut then follows that command until you give it a different command.
  • **Guard** The hut watches for trespassers within 120 feet using your Perception modifier and screams if it spots any.
  • **Lock** Each entrance to the hut is sealed with a [_lock_](/Spells.aspx?ID=174) spell.
  • **Move** The hut gains a Speed of 60 feet, growing giant bird or bone legs, if necessary, and follows an extremely basic movement command you give it, such as “follow me” or “move that direction.” While perfectly suitable for overland travel, the hut's broad movements and 1-round delay on response time are too imprecise to predictably direct in a combat encounter or other situation where seconds and precise locations count.
  • **Hide** The hut appears to be a normal, mundane object of its type. This is a 10th-level illusion effect.
You can have only one hut at a time. If you animate a new hut, your previous hut immediately reverts to its original, mundane form. If you die, the hut continues following the last order you gave it indefinitely.

fields.text: Feat 20 Witch's Hut Witch Source Advanced Player's Guide pg. 105 Your home is an animated structure that obeys your commands. By performing a rite that takes 1 day, you create an animated object from a hut, small house, covered wagon, tent, or similar construction of up to Huge size. The hut uses your AC, saving throw modifiers, and Perception modifier and has 150 HP and Hardness 10. It has the construct armor ability, meaning once it's reduced to less than half its Hit Points, or immediately upon being damaged by a critical hit, its AC is reduced by 4 until it is repaired. The hut can't attack or attempt skill checks. You can give the hut a command as a single action, which has the auditory and concentrate traits; after 1 round of reconfiguring itself, the hut then follows that command until you give it a different command. Guard The hut watches for trespassers within 120 feet using your Perception modifier and screams if it spots any. Lock Each entrance to the hut is sealed with a lock spell. Move The hut gains a Speed of 60 feet, growing giant bird or bone legs, if necessary, and follows an extremely basic movement command you give it, such as “follow me” or “move that direction.” While perfectly suitable for overland travel, the hut's broad movements and 1-round delay on response time are too imprecise to predictably direct in a combat encounter or other situation where seconds and precise locations count. Hide The hut appears to be a normal, mundane object of its type. This is a 10th-level illusion effect. You can have only one hut at a time. If you animate a new hut, your previous hut immediately reverts to its original, mundane form. If you die, the hut continues following the last order you gave it indefinitely.

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 35 --- You touch a creature to implant a malignant seed in its body. The creature takes 5d10 piercing damage and other effects depending on its Fortitude save against your class DC. The creature is then temporarily immune for 24 hours. Creatures with the [fungus](/Traits.aspx?ID=77), [plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=125), or [wood](/Traits.aspx?ID=508) trait are immune. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.

**Failure** The target takes full damage and is [clumsy 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=3) and [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24) until the end of its next turn.
**Critical Failure** The target takes double damage and is clumsy 2 and immobilized. It attempts a new save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect if it succeeds. --- **Level (+4)** The damage increases by 1d10.

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 108 **Archetype** [Apocalypse Rider](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=287) **Frequency** once per 10 minutes **Prerequisites** [Apocalypse Rider Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7304); [Battle Harbinger Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7505) --- You hasten the passage of time for a living creature, prematurely aging them into decrepitude. A living creature within 60 feet takes 14d6 [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) damage and a part of its body you chose withers, taking the following penalties depending on the result of their a Fortitude saving throw against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher.
  • **Arms** The target’s arms grow weak. The target becomes [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71) 1.
  • **Head** The target has trouble thinking straight. The target becomes [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1.
  • **Legs** The target’s legs buckle with every movement. The target takes a –10-foot status penalty to its Speeds.
  • **Torso** The target’s skin becomes thin and papery. The target gains [weakness](/Rules.aspx?ID=2317) 10 to slashing damage.
**Critical Success** The target is unaffected.
**Success** The target takes half damage and the withering penalty lasts until the end of your next turn.
**Failure** The creature takes full damage and the withering penalty lasts for 1 minute.
**Critical Failure** The creature takes double damage, and you can choose a second part of the body to wither. Both penalties last for 1 minute.

<column gap="tiny">

---

With a bit of hide, some antlers, and some cast-off fur, you can create a disguise that will fool even an experienced hunter. You can [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46) creatures with the [animal](/Traits.aspx?ID=9), [beast](/Traits.aspx?ID=20), or [plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=125) traits, so long as they are either the same size or one size larger than you and have a body shape that conforms at least vaguely to your own (in other words, a typical humanoid could Impersonate a [bear](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=13) or an [arboreal](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=8), but not a [horse](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=62), [giant scorpion](/Monsters.aspx?ID=356), or [assassin vine](/Monsters.aspx?ID=555)). Impersonating a larger creature doesn't change your actual size.

_Nethys Note: This is a part of the April Fool's content from Paizo's blogs._

You make a quick attack before retreating to safety. You either make a wombat butt [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) or [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=2380) an adjacent creature, after which you can [Step](/Actions.aspx?ID=2304) and [Take Cover](/Actions.aspx?ID=2307). >
[Wonder Worker](/Feats.aspx?ID=3735) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Thaumaturge" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=432" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 47

**Prerequisites**
Legendary in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), Legendary in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10), Legendary in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11), or Legendary in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13)

</column>

---

The thaumaturge's path culminates with the working of wonders. Once per day, you can align your esoterica to cast a spell of 8th level or lower that takes 1, 2, or 3 actions to cast. The spell must be common or one to which you have access. You can choose a spell of any tradition for which you're legendary in the associated skill (Arcana for [arcane](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=1), Nature for [primal](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=4), Occultism for [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3), or Religion for [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2)). Use your thaumaturge class DC in place of any necessary spell DC and your thaumaturge class DC – 10 in place of any necessary [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) modifier or spell attack modifier.

>
[Wood Ward](/Feats.aspx?ID=4323) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Ardande" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=498" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Plant" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=125" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
<trait label="Wood" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=508" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 49

**Frequency**
once per hour

**Trigger**
A creature targets you with an attack.

</column>

---

With a sweep of your hand, vines and roots burst from the ground along the edge of your space between you and the attacker, creating a natural lattice of wood that grants [standard cover](/Rules.aspx?ID=459). The circumstance bonus from the cover applies to your AC when you're determining the outcome of the triggering attack. If the triggering attack still hits and deals physical damage to you, the ward reduces the damage by 30 and is immediately destroyed. </title>

<traits>

<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Overflow" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=506" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
<trait label="Wood" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=508" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 34

</column>

---

Planks of wood, embellished with carvings, spring forth to form a wall. The palisade is up to 30 feet long, 20 feet high, and 1 inch thick. It must form within 120 feet in a straight line in an unbroken open space that doesn't pass through any creatures or objects, or the impulse fails. When you create the wall, you can choose to create ledges on one side of the wall, 4 feet from the top, with ladders reaching to them from the bottom of the wall.

 Each 10-foot-by-10-foot section of the wall has AC 10, Hardness 10, and 20 Hit Points, and is immune to critical hits and precision damage. The wall lasts until the end of your next turn, but you can Sustain it up to 1 minute.

---
**Level (+2)** The maximum length of the wall increases by 10 feet, and the HP of each section increase by 10.

You have unlocked abstruse methods to tangle with reality itself, altering the fate of a single individual. <title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[World Rouser Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=9376) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 106

**Archetype** [World Rouser](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=396)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)

</column>

---

You know how to wake the world around you from its slumber, whether through your natural affinity for nature or hard-earned knowledge. You gain the Rouse the World action. 

As your ability to converse with the world grows, you can call on it to help you in other ways, some of which require a saving throw. The DC for an ability gained via this archetype is either your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher, and is called your world rouser DC.

**Rouse the World** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) The flora, fauna, and elements in a 10- foot burst within 30 feet stir, aiding you and your allies and whispering in your ear. This area is known as your waking world. While in your waking world, you and your allies gain a +1 circumstance bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) and [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) checks, and you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) checks to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) about creatures and hazards in the area. The effect lasts for 10 minutes, but you can [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) it. Once per round on subsequent turns, you can [Sustain](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) this ability to increase the burst’s size by 10 feet. You can Rouse the World in only one area at a time; if you use this ability again, the first area returns to normal.

<title level="2">World Rouser Dedication leads to...</title>
[A Hush Falls Over the World](/Feats.aspx?ID=9383), [All Returns to Slumber](/Feats.aspx?ID=9379), [Awake With a Roar](/Feats.aspx?ID=9386), [Come in From the Wilderness](/Feats.aspx?ID=9384), [Dust Cloud](/Feats.aspx?ID=9381), [Nature's Embrace](/Feats.aspx?ID=9377), [Sheltering Hand](/Feats.aspx?ID=9380), [The World Devours](/Feats.aspx?ID=9385), [The World Whispers](/Feats.aspx?ID=9378), [Wake and Tremble](/Feats.aspx?ID=9382)

fields.text: Feat 14 World-breaking Footfall Two Actions Monk Source Tian Xia Character Guide pg. 121 Prerequisites Kaiju Stance Requirements You are in Kaiju Stance and are touching the ground. You slam the ground and unleash a fearsome roar, sending broken shards of earth flying in all directions. The ground in a 20-foot emanation around you becomes difficult terrain, or greater difficult terrain if it was already difficult terrain. All other creatures within the emanation take 7d6 bludgeoning damage with a basic Reflex save against your class DC. You then can’t use World-breaking Footfall for 1d4 rounds.

---

Through your spiritual power, you impede starvation and restore pantries. You can cast [_create food_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1475) and [_cleanse cuisine_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1468) as 2nd-rank [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676) innate spells, each once per day. Additionally, when you cast these spells, you instantly restore Hit Points to the containers storing these magical comestibles as though you’ve succeeded at a [Repair](/Actions.aspx?ID=2384) action using your proficiency in your spell DC in place of your [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) proficiency.

If your next action is to Cast a Spell of at least 5th level from your spell slots that affects an area, you can apply one of the following planar effects to a 20-foot burst centered within the spell's area. The effect persists for 1 minute.
  • **Gravitational Morass** The pull of gravity is amplified here, creating greater difficult terrain. [Flying](/Actions.aspx?ID=94) creatures that pass through the area must succeed at a Reflex save against your spell DC or fall to the ground, taking bludgeoning damage equal to half the distance fallen.
  • **Flowing Time** Erratic timestreams aid you within this space. A creature that starts its turn in the burst is affected by [_haste_](/Spells.aspx?ID=147) on that turn.

**Source** [Pathfinder #194: Cult of the Cave Worm](/Sources.aspx?ID=209) pg. 80

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Shake it Off is a reaction_

**Archetype** [Worm Caller](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=208)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) or Trained in [Cave Worm Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8)

</column>

---

You pledge yourself to understanding and emulating one of the most powerful creatures of the Darklands: the mighty [cave worm](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=21). You gain the following action.

 **Shake It Off** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=76), [primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=134)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You fail or critically fail a saving throw against a condition or adverse effect (such as [_baleful polymorph_](/Spells.aspx?ID=17)); **Effect** You reroll the triggering save and use the better result.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the Worm Caller archetype.

<title level="2">Worm Caller Dedication leads to...</title>
[Azure Fins](/Feats.aspx?ID=4363), [Call Worm Spirit](/Feats.aspx?ID=4364), [Crimson Breath](/Feats.aspx?ID=4366), [Inexorable](/Feats.aspx?ID=4360), [Tunnel](/Feats.aspx?ID=4365), [Venomous Touch](/Feats.aspx?ID=4367), [Worm Empathy](/Feats.aspx?ID=4362), [Worm Form](/Feats.aspx?ID=4368), [Worm Sense](/Feats.aspx?ID=4358), [Worm's Feast](/Feats.aspx?ID=4361), [Wormskin](/Feats.aspx?ID=4359)

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Pathfinder #194: Cult of the Cave Worm](/Sources.aspx?ID=209) pg. 81 **Archetype** [Worm Caller](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=208) **Prerequisites** [Worm Caller Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=4357) --- You take on the form of a purple worm or transform into a humanoid-worm hybrid, retaining your own head but with a worm's body, transforming into a Huge battle form. You must have enough space to expand into or the ability is lost. While in this form, you gain the [animal](/Traits.aspx?ID=9) trait. You can Dismiss the form. You gain the following statistics and abilities regardless of which battle form you choose:
  • AC = 20 + your level. Ignore your armor's check penalty and Speed reduction.
  • 40 temporary Hit Points.
  • [Darkvision](/Rules.aspx?ID=415).
  • One or more [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) melee attacks specific to the battle form you choose, which are the only attacks you can Strike with. You're trained with them. Your attack modifier is +25, and you use the listed damage. Melee attacks are Strength based (for the purpose of the [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13) condition, for example). If your unarmed attack modifier is higher, you can use it instead.
  • [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) modifier of +30, unless your own modifier is higher.
You also gain specific abilities based on the type of monster you choose:
  • **Purple Worm** Speed 40 feet, burrow 30 feet, swim 20 feet; **Melee** jaws ([deadly 2d10](/Traits.aspx?ID=174), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 3d10+15 piercing; **Melee** stinger ([agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d12+15 piercing plus 2d6 [persistent poison](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29); **Melee** body ([reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)) **Damage** 1d10+13 bludgeoning
  • **Hybrid** Speed 40 feet; **Melee** stinger ([agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 2d12+15 piercing plus 1d6 [persistent poison](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29); **Melee** body ([reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=192)), **Damage** 1d10+13 bludgeoning; **Hybrid Caster** You retain the ability to speak, and can cast spells as long as they don't have somatic or material components.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Wormskin](/Feats.aspx?ID=4359) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #194: Cult of the Cave Worm](/Sources.aspx?ID=209) pg. 80

**Archetype** [Worm Caller](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=208)

**Prerequisites**
[Worm Caller Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=4357)

</column>

---

Your flesh grows thick and bloated, protecting you against harm. You gain resistance equal to half your level versus one of the following types of damage, chosen when you take the feat: fire, cold, or bludgeoning. This choice cannot be changed.

 When you're unarmored, your flesh gives you a +2 item bonus to AC with a Dexterity cap of +3. You can apply with armor potency runes and property runes directly to your flesh, though excruciatingly painful.

**Special** You can take this feat up to three times, each time selecting a new damage type from the list.

[Wortwitch](/Feats.aspx?ID=1564) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Witch" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=323" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 101

</column>

---

You have a particular affinity for leafy plants. Your patron grants you a leshy familiar. If you already had a familiar, this leshy replaces your previous familiar, as if your previous familiar had been slain. In addition, you gain the ability to see through leaves, vines, and other foliage. You don't take circumstance penalties to ranged spell attacks or Perception checks caused by foliage, and your targeted attacks don't require a flat check to succeed against a target [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) only by such vegetation.

>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

**Archetype** [Pure Legion Enforcer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=377)

**Prerequisites**
[Pure Legion Enforcer Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8891)

</column>

---

You channel your commitment to removing the divine from the world as you recite the Laws of Mortality. Strike a foe that can cast divine spells. The Strike deals two extra weapon damage dice. The target must also attempt a Will save against your class DC. On a failure, it loses its highest-rank available divine spell prepared or its highest unused spell slot to cast a divine spell. If it has multiple spells at its highest rank available, it randomly selects which spell is lost. On a critical failure, it also can't cast divine spells until the start of your next turn.

The ravenous maggots inside you become capable of exploding forth from your attacks into the wounds of an opponent, whispering telepathic words of destruction that invoke horrific flashbacks of Kabriri's transformation from [elf](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=371) to [ghoul](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=52) or psychic images of hundreds of maggots bursting from the victim's flesh all at once. Make a melee Strike against a target creature. If it hits, in addition to taking damage from the Strike, the target is affected by a 10th-level casting of [_power word kill_](/Spells.aspx?ID=227). If Wrath of the First Ghoul is used against a target [elf](/Traits.aspx?ID=58), [Leng ghoul](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1165), or worshipper of [Pharasma](/Deities.aspx?ID=14) and does not instantly kill the creature, the target takes double damage.

Your training in the wrestling arts has made you particularly adept at moving, striking, and grappling while unencumbered. </title>

<traits>
<trait label="Arcane" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=11" />
<trait label="Flourish" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=73" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star](/Sources.aspx?ID=283) pg. 74

**Archetype** [Avenging Runelord](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=338)

**Prerequisites**
[Avenging Runelord Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8139)

**Requirements**
You are wielding a polearm or spear.

</column>

---

Your prowess with long-hafted weapons catches your opponents by surprise, as it bends or elongates in an obviously supernatural manner. Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3323). Your weapon gains the [reach](/Traits.aspx?ID=684) trait until the end of your turn, if it doesn’t have it already. You can Stride and Strike twice, in any order. The movement from your Stride doesn’t provoke reactions. Your Strikes are made at mythic proficiency and gain the critical specialization effect of the weapon. Apply your [multiple attack penalty](/Rules.aspx?ID=2289) to your Strikes as normal, but the target of your second Strike is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) to it.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Writing on the Wall](/Feats.aspx?ID=9186) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Runesmith" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=952" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 49

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), Expert in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43), Expert in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44), or Expert in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)

</column>

---

You place hidden messages written in a runic cipher of your devising. You can cast [_embed message_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1511) once per day as an [innate spell](/Rules.aspx?ID=2232). The rank of this spell is equal to half your level, rounded up, and the tradition can be any tradition for which you are at least expert in the related skill (Arcana for [arcane](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=1), Nature for [primal](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=4), Occultism for [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3), and Religion for [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2)). When you cast _embed message_, instead of choosing a language you know for the message’s text and speech, you can choose to have the message be text only, written in a runic code that only you know. You can impart the knowledge of this code to up to 5 creatures over the course of 10 minutes; they retain this knowledge indefinitely, but you can devise a new runic code for subsequent messages you wish to be encoded.

A creature can [Decipher the Writing](/Actions.aspx?ID=2363) of your runic code using the same skill associated with the chosen tradition against your class DC.

You gain the [_wronged monk's wrath_](/Spells.aspx?ID=849) ki spell. Increase the number of Focus Points in your focus pool by 1.

<title level="2">Feats</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #166: Despair on Danger Island](/Sources.aspx?ID=85) pg. 74

The player characters might learn some of these techniques from friends and rivals during their stay on Bonmu, allowing them to select the feats the next time they would gain a feat. Surviving combat against Syu Tak-nwa allows the characters to take the three witch feats, while defeating or impressing the Ahmoza twins allows them to take Entwined Energy Ki. <title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Xidao Sea Mine Drop](/Feats.aspx?ID=7077) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Inventor" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=408" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 110

**Prerequisites**
[Diving Armor](/Feats.aspx?ID=3056)

**Access**
Tian Xia origin

</column>

---

You've rigged your armor innovation with a gizmo that can safely synthesize two sea mines a day, holding them in a protected compartment. You must be submerged in water to use this action, and the mines only detonate if they're underwater. 

You off-load a mine onto an unoccupied square within your reach. The mine is primed to explode when a Small or larger creature moves into its square, or when you Interact to Activate your gizmo's remote detonation button, which explodes a single mine up to 50 feet away. As a 1-minute activity, you can hide a mine. Creatures can detect a hidden mine as they would any trap or hazard, using your Craft DC as the Stealth DC. If you don't Conceal the mine, its position is obvious.

Any creature in a 5-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) around the mine when it detonates takes 3d4 bludgeoning damage and 1d4 piercing damage, with a basic Reflex save against your class DC. The bludgeoning damage of your mines increases by 1d4 at 8th level and every 2 levels thereafter. Any mines that haven't detonated when you make your daily preparations become inert and harmless.

**Unstable Function** You push the safety limits of your gizmo, forcing it to synthesize and launch additional sea mines, exceeding the daily limit. Add the [unstable](/Traits.aspx?ID=416) trait to Xidao Sea Mine Drop. You create up to 3 additional sea mines that you can immediately deploy in different unoccupied spaces up to 30 feet away.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 119

**Archetype** [Beast Lord](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=290)

**Prerequisites**
[Beast Lord Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7345)

**Requirements**
Your united [companion](/Traits.aspx?ID=558) made a successful [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) against a creature this round.

</column>

---

When you and your [companion](/Traits.aspx?ID=558) attack together, you can ensure that escape is but a whispered dream. [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) the same creature that your united companion hit. If your Strike is successful, the targeted creature has been marked for death by you and your companion and can’t become [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79) or [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) to you and your companion for 1 minute or until it moves more than 60 feet away from either you or your companion, whichever comes first. If the triggering creature is under an effect or spell that would normally grant it this condition, you can immediately attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) the effect. Your counteract rank is half your level rounded up, and your counteract check modifier is equal to the higher of your class DC –10 or spell DC –10.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 20"
    pfs=""
>
[You Can't Kill an Idea](/Feats.aspx?ID=7373) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 125

**Archetype** [Broken Chain](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=291)

**Prerequisites**
[Broken Chain Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7357)

</column>

---

Those who would destroy you instead transform you into a powerful yet formless entity. If you would be killed while you have an [Ultimatum of Liberation](/Actions.aspx?ID=2993) active, you (along with your equipment) become an ideaform.

As an ideaform, you are [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=83) and [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=632). You have only 1 Hit Point and can’t gain more, but you are [immune](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) to all damage; if your [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) or [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67) condition would increase to a high enough value to kill you, it does not increase, and you are immune to any effect that would instantly kill or destroy you. You are immune to the [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) condition, yet can take only purely [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) actions. You can communicate telepathically with your allies at unlimited range, and gain two extra reactions at the start of each of your turns. Additionally, you can [Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=2292) allies through nothing but telepathic advice, without having to spend an action to prepare first, and can spend a Mythic Point to do so at mythic proficiency. Any circumstance bonus you grant through Aiding is increased by 1.

Before an hour passes while being an ideaform, you must choose a willing follower of your cause to fuse with and cease to be an ideaform. Use your level, their [ancestry](/Rules.aspx?ID=3286), [heritage](/Rules.aspx?ID=2083), and [ancestry feats](/Rules.aspx?ID=2084), and work with your GM to choose which combination of class, attribute modifiers, skills, and feats would make a good representation of this fusion. This new character has all your previous equipment. If you do not fuse with a follower after an hour of being an ideaform, you cease to be an ideaform and die; the equipment you had at the time of your original death also ceases to exist.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 16"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[You Failed to Account for… This!](/Feats.aspx?ID=3084) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Inventor" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=408" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 31

**Trigger**
A creature you can see targets you with an attack against your AC.

</column>

---

When your foes try to attack you, you always seem to have some outlandish invention you can pull out at the last second to protect you from whatever attack they throw at you. Describe a device you’re attempting to use to protect yourself from the foe’s attack—for instance, when attacked by an [elemental hurricane's](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2976) lightning lash Strike, you might pull out a specially grounded lightning rod from that time you tried to power an invention by harnessing a thunderstorm! Using an invention to defend in this way means that the attack roll for the triggering attack targets your [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) DC instead of your AC.

Since you’re using your Crafting DC instead of your AC, any penalties to your AC don’t apply, but this doesn’t remove any conditions or other effects that are causing you such penalties. For instance, if you were [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) and used an invention to defend against a sneak attack, you’d still take the extra precision damage if you were hit, even though the –2 penalty to AC from being off-guard wouldn’t apply to your Crafting DC.

fields.text: Feat 16 You Failed to Account for… This! Reaction Inventor Source Guns & Gears (Remastered) pg. 31 Trigger A creature you can see targets you with an attack against your AC. When your foes try to attack you, you always seem to have some outlandish invention you can pull out at the last second to protect you from whatever attack they throw at you. Describe a device you’re attempting to use to protect yourself from the foe’s attack—for instance, when attacked by an elemental hurricane's lightning lash Strike, you might pull out a specially grounded lightning rod from that time you tried to power an invention by harnessing a thunderstorm! Using an invention to defend in this way means that the attack roll for the triggering attack targets your Crafting DC instead of your AC. Since you’re using your Crafting DC instead of your AC, any penalties to your AC don’t apply, but this doesn’t remove any conditions or other effects that are causing you such penalties. For instance, if you were off-guard and used an invention to defend against a sneak attack, you’d still take the extra precision damage if you were hit, even though the –2 penalty to AC from being off-guard wouldn’t apply to your Crafting DC.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 16"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[You Failed to Account for… This!](/Feats.aspx?ID=8586) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Inventor" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=408" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears](/Sources.aspx?ID=318) pg. 32

**Trigger**
A creature you can see targets you with an attack against your AC.

</column>

---

When your foes try to attack you, you always seem to have some outlandish invention you can pull out at the last second to protect you from whatever attack they throw at you. Describe a device you’re attempting to use to protect yourself from the foe’s attack—for instance, when attacked by a [shocker lizard](/Monsters.aspx?ID=802)’s shock Strike, you might pull out a specially grounded lightning rod from that time you tried to power an invention by harnessing a thunderstorm! Using an invention to defend in this way means that the attack roll for the triggering attack targets your [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) DC instead of your AC.

Since you’re using your Crafting DC instead of your AC, any penalties to your AC don’t apply, but this doesn’t remove any conditions or other effects that are causing you such penalties. For instance, if you were [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) and used an invention to defend against a sneak attack, you’d still take the extra precision damage if you were hit, even though the –2 penalty to AC from being flat-footed wouldn’t apply to your Crafting DC.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Fortune" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=76" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Firebrands](/Sources.aspx?ID=196) pg. 79

**Archetype** [Celebrity](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=245)

**Prerequisites**
Celebrity Archetype 

**Access**
Members of the Firebrands at the rank of second mark or higher have access to this feat.

**Trigger**
An ally within 30 feet fails a Will saving throw against an [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93) effect.

</column>

---

Some Firebrands can't stand it when their allies are ruining their moment, and you're no different. Your loud and forceful condemnation of an ally succumbing to an incapacitation effect gives them a second chance to impress you and shake off the effect. Your ally rerolls the triggering Will saving throw with a +1 circumstance bonus. Regardless of the result of the save, your ally is temporarily immune to You're an Embarrassment! for 10 minutes.

    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"

[Zealous Inevitability](/Feats.aspx?ID=7233) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Flourish" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=606" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 59

**Archetype** [Avenger](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=282)

**Prerequisites**
[Avenger Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7232)

**Requirements**
You are wielding your deity’s [favored weapon](/Rules.aspx?ID=805)

</column>

---

You channel your zeal through a sacred weapon, bringing a foe closer to their demise. [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) a target with the required weapon. On a success, the target becomes [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67) 1 or increases the value of their doomed condition by 1 (most living creatures die when they’ve reached doomed 4). Creatures doomed in this way take a status penalty to their saving throws against [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579) spells equal to their doomed value. 

A creature that would become doomed 4 by this Strike can attempt a Will saving throw against your class DC to avoid increasing the value of their doomed condition. When this occurs, this ability gains the [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=631) trait.

---

As a Zephyr Guard, you’re always vigilant against crime and threats to the city’s safety. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Perception checks against attempts to [Palm an Object](/Actions.aspx?ID=67), [Steal](/Actions.aspx?ID=68), or [Conceal an Object](/Actions.aspx?ID=61) (including you’re [Seeking](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) concealed objects). You become trained in [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14) and Katapesh [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8); if you were already trained, you become an expert instead.

**Special** You can’t select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the Zephyr Guard archetype.

<title level="2">Zephyr Guard Dedication leads to...</title>
[Decry Thief](/Feats.aspx?ID=1155), [Know the Beat](/Feats.aspx?ID=1156), [Relentless Disarm](/Feats.aspx?ID=1157), [Unfazed Assessment](/Feats.aspx?ID=1158)

<title

    right="Feat 2"

>
[Zombie Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3557) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 60

**Archetype** [Zombie](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=182)

**Prerequisites**
You died and were animated as a [husk zombie](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1919).

</column>

---

Despite your death and subsequent reanimation as a rotting corpse, you retain most of your mind and identity. Yet, it's always there: the hunger for the flesh and organs of the living. You gain the [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) and [zombie](/Traits.aspx?ID=245) traits, and the [basic undead benefits](/Rules.aspx?ID=1694). Unlike a typical zombie, you're not mindless. Reduce all your Speeds by 5 feet. Your fist loses the nonlethal trait.

 Because of its progressing state of decay, your body requires continual maintenance to remain at its best. Each day after your rest period, your body is deteriorated due to natural decay. Additionally, some zombie abilities allow you to push for a greater effect in exchange for a chance of deteriorating your body.

 While your body is deteriorated, you're [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35). You can spend 10 minutes checking and repairing your joints and other weak parts of your body to recover from deterioration. You can perform these repairs as part of your daily preparations. Because it's a natural result of your body's functions, you can't remove the slowed condition from deterioration through any other means.

 You crave the flesh of the living. You gain a jaws unarmed attack that deals 1d8 piercing damage. Your jaws are in the [brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) group and have the [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) trait. You can use your jaws Strike only against a creature that's [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=33) by you.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the zombie archetype.

<title level="2">Zombie Dedication leads to...</title>
[Ankle Biter](/Feats.aspx?ID=3558), [Feast](/Feats.aspx?ID=3559), [Festering Wound](/Feats.aspx?ID=3566), [Numb](/Feats.aspx?ID=3562), [Out of Hand](/Feats.aspx?ID=3563), [Ravenous Charge](/Feats.aspx?ID=3560), [Seize](/Feats.aspx?ID=3567), [Shamble](/Feats.aspx?ID=3564), [Unkillable](/Feats.aspx?ID=3565)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 20"
    pfs=""
>
[Zombie Horde](/Feats.aspx?ID=3654) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #180: The Smoking Gun](/Sources.aspx?ID=125) pg. 79

**Archetype** [Clockwork Reanimator](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=184)

**Prerequisites**
[Clockwork Reanimator Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3645)

</column>

---

You built your reanimated construct companion of modular components from various corpses. Its unique makeup enables your companion to split into dozens or even hundreds of much smaller corpse constructs. Acting as one, this shambling swarm can overwhelm your enemies. 

You Command your reanimated construct companion. Instead of its normal actions, the companion splits into a horde of Small and Tiny construct companions within a 30-foot emanation from its original space. The horde makes a Strike against each foe within the emanation with a +2 circumstance bonus to its attack rolls. The multiple attack penalty doesn't increase until after the companion makes all the attacks. The miniature companions recombine into a single companion of their original size at any location within the emanation.

<traits>

---

Your studies have expanded your ability to parley and negotiate into the animal realm. You can [Request](/Actions.aspx?ID=2393) from [animals](/Traits.aspx?ID=531) using [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) instead of [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) as though you shared a language, although this gives you no special ability to understand their responses. You can also use Performance instead of [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) to [Command an Animal](/Actions.aspx?ID=2400).
